name: GeminiImageGen
title: Gemini Image Gen
description: Generate images using Google's Gemini models
whenToUse: Pick to CREATE an image from a description: a picture, illustration, photo or graphic that does not exist yet. Returns the rendered image data itself rather than a description of one, and can take a reference photo to keep a person recognisable across several generations. Editing an image that already exists, and producing a fixed branded template, are different jobs.

package.name: gce-toolkit
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# GEMINI IMAGE GENERATION AS A MANIFEST. Needed nothing new: an api-key header, a JSON POST,
# and `transport: binary` for the optional reference photo, which S3Upload had already forced.
#
# TWO THINGS CHANGED, both recorded on the node itself:
#
#   the instruction text  The retired service held two long instruction strings inline. They
#                         are prompt BLOCKS now, because a node holding a copy of words that
#                         also live in a block is a copy that drifts.
#   generateContent       The retired service used the SDK's generateContentStream and
#                         accumulated the chunks. This asks the non-streaming endpoint for the
#                         same thing, so the node still settles once and stays a PromiseNode.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/gce-toolkit/`.

name: gce-toolkit
displayName: Google Gemini
description: Generate images with Google Gemini models
version: 2.0.0
category: media
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1768126954/gravity/icons/gemini.png

features:
  - Text to image, several images per request
  - An optional reference photo, used for facial likeness only
  - The model's own text response alongside the images

allowedHosts:
  - generativelanguage.googleapis.com
  # Any host, for the UNAUTHENTICATED reference-photo fetch only. The url is one a person
  # supplies, so it cannot be declared in advance. That call sends no credential, and the
  # executor refuses "*" the moment one does.
  - "*"

requires:
  credential: [apiKeyHeader]
  transport: [json, binary]
  executorVersion: ">=1.4.0"

credentials.geminiCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# Transcribed from the retired GeminiCredential, NAME AND FIELD UNCHANGED so credentials
# already stored against `geminiCredential` keep resolving.

name: geminiCredential
displayName: Google Gemini
description: Credentials for the Google Gemini API
documentationUrl: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/api-key

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Google Gemini API key
    placeholder: AIza...

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.
#
# All three read the same parts list. Gemini mixes image parts and text parts in one array, so
# each row filters for the kind it wants rather than assuming a position.
#
# `inlineData` OR `inline_data`: the REST reference documents snake_case and the JSON mapping
# accepts both, so which one comes back is not something a manifest should bet on.

- emit: images
  from: response
  value: >-
    return ((((((calls.generate || {}).candidates || [])[0] || {}).content || {}).parts) || [])
      .filter(p => p.inlineData || p.inline_data)
      .map((p, i) => ({
        data: (p.inlineData || p.inline_data || {}).data || '',
        mimeType: (p.inlineData || p.inline_data || {}).mimeType
          || (p.inlineData || p.inline_data || {}).mime_type
          || 'image/png',
        fileName: String(config.fileName || 'generated_image') + '_' + i + '.'
          + String((p.inlineData || p.inline_data || {}).mimeType
              || (p.inlineData || p.inline_data || {}).mime_type
              || 'image/png')
              .split('/').at(-1).split('+')[0]
      }))

- emit: text
  from: response
  value: >-
    return ((((((calls.generate || {}).candidates || [])[0] || {}).content || {}).parts) || [])
      .filter(p => typeof p.text === 'string')
      .map(p => p.text)
      .join('')

# `generatedAt` is EPOCH MILLISECONDS, where the retired node emitted an ISO string. The
# sandbox exposes Date.now() and refuses `new`, so there is no way to format a date inside an
# expression. Renamed from `timestamp` rather than kept with a different type under the same
# name, because a downstream template doing string work on an ISO date would otherwise break
# silently on a number.
- emit: metadata
  from: response
  value: >-
    return {
      model: config.model,
      imageCount: ((((((calls.generate || {}).candidates || [])[0] || {}).content || {}).parts) || [])
        .filter(p => p.inlineData || p.inline_data).length,
      generatedAt: Date.now()
    }
files.api/run.yaml:
# Fetch the reference photo (sometimes), then generate.
#
# The first call is skipped when no reference url is set, so the common case is one request.

# NO AUTH, which is why `*` is in allowedHosts. The url is one a person supplies and cannot be
# declared in advance; this call carries no credential, so there is nothing to leak, and https
# is still required.
#
# DELIBERATELY NOT FATAL. The retired service caught a failed reference fetch and carried on
# without the photo, on the reasoning that a generated image is better than no image. `error`
# is therefore absent here: a 404 leaves `calls.reference` unset and every expression below
# already treats that as "no photo was given".
- name: reference
  when: "return !!String(config.referenceImageUrl || '').trim()"
  method: GET
  url: "{{ config.referenceImageUrl }}"
  # { base64, contentType, bytes }, which is exactly the shape an inline image part needs.
  transport: binary
  timeoutMs: 60000

- name: generate
  method: POST
  url: >-
    return 'https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/'
      + config.model + ':generateContent'
  credential:
    scheme: apiKeyHeader
    header: x-goog-api-key
    value: "{{ credentials.geminiCredential.apiKey }}"
  headers:
    Content-Type: application/json
  transport: json
  # Image generation is slow, and the pro model more so. The retired node inherited the SDK's
  # default; this states one rather than leaving it to whatever the platform's happens to be.
  timeoutMs: 300000
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

  body:
    contents:
      - role: user
        # The photo FIRST, then the text. Order matters to the model: the instruction that
        # follows an image is read as being about that image.
        #
        # `prompt.geminiLikenessPreface` is reached as an expression root rather than as
        # {{prompt.…}}, because handlebars cannot be spliced into the middle of an expression.
        # Same block either way.
        parts: >-
          return [].concat(calls.reference
              ? [{ inline_data: {
                    mime_type: calls.reference.contentType || 'image/jpeg',
                    data: calls.reference.base64
                  } }]
              : [])
            .concat([{ text: (calls.reference ? prompt.geminiLikenessPreface + '\n\n' : '')
              + String(config.prompt || '') }])

    # Only sent when there IS a photo, because it is entirely about how to treat one.
    # `undefined` drops the key when the body is serialised, which is what "not sent" means
    # here; null would be sent and rejected.
    systemInstruction: >-
      return calls.reference
        ? { parts: [{ text: prompt.geminiLikenessSystem }] }
        : undefined

    generationConfig:
      # BOTH modalities, not just IMAGE. These models answer with a parts list that mixes
      # inline image data and text, and asking for image alone makes the text response
      # unavailable rather than merely unused.
      responseModalities: [IMAGE, TEXT]

  error:
    # Gemini reports a refused prompt as a 200 with candidates present and no image part in
    # them, so status alone cannot tell success from a safety block. `finishReason` is where it
    # says so, and without this the node would emit an empty images array and look like it
    # worked.
    when: >-
      return !((((((response.candidates || [])[0] || {}).content || {}).parts) || [])
        .filter(p => p.inlineData || p.inline_data).length)
    message: >-
      return 'Gemini returned no image. finishReason: '
        + String(((response.candidates || [])[0] || {}).finishReason || 'unknown')
        + (response.promptFeedback ? ' promptFeedback: ' + JSON.stringify(response.promptFeedback) : '')
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [model, prompt]
  properties:
    model:
      type: string
      title: Model
      description: Which Gemini image model to generate with
      enum:
        - gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview
        - gemini-3-pro-image-preview
        - gemini-2.5-flash-image
      enumNames:
        - Gemini 3.1 Flash Image (best for character consistency)
        - Gemini 3 Pro (Nano Banana Pro)
        - Gemini 2.5 Flash Image (Nano Banana)
      default: gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview
    prompt:
      type: string
      title: Image Prompt
      description: Describe the image to generate. Shared blocks work here, e.g. {{prompt.geminiLikenessPreface}}.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
      "ui:ai":
        editable: true
    fileName:
      type: string
      title: File Name Prefix
      description: Prefixes each generated file name, which is then numbered and given an extension
      default: generated_image
      "ui:field": template
    referenceImageUrl:
      type: string
      title: Reference Image URL
      description: >-
        A photo to take facial likeness from. Leave empty to generate from the prompt alone.
        When set, the model is told the photo is a casting reference and the prompt still
        directs the scene.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template

    # WHO MAY RUN THIS BOX, set by whoever builds the workflow (15-who-can-run-it.md).
    #
    # INSTANCE config, not the manifest's `auth`, and the two answer different questions.
    # The manifest is the node author's FLOOR: "this node is inherently privileged". These
    # are the builder's, per box on the canvas, because the same node type legitimately
    # faces staff on one workflow and customers on another.
    #
    # A role especially has to live here: `finance:approve` is a claim THIS deployment's
    # identity provider mints, and a node published to the marketplace cannot know the role
    # vocabulary of every universe that installs it.
    #
    # The executor takes the STRICTER of the two. Neither can loosen the other.
    authRequired:
      type: boolean
      title: Require sign-in
      description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    authRole:
      type: string
      title: Require role
      description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { authRequired: true }

"ui:order": [authRequired, authRole, model, prompt, fileName, referenceImageUrl]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Data from previous nodes, referenceable in the prompt and reference url
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: images
    type: array
    description: >-
      One entry per image: data (base64), mimeType, fileName. Index first when reading one,
      e.g. images.0.data
  - name: text
    type: string
    description: Anything the model said alongside the images, often empty
  - name: metadata
    type: object
    description: model, imageCount, generatedAt

credentials:
  - name: geminiCredential
    required: true
    displayName: Google Gemini API
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: GeminiImageGen
kind: PromiseNode

name: Gemini Image Gen
category: Media & Design
color: "#4285F4"

description: Generate images using Google's Gemini models

whenToUse: >-
  Pick to CREATE an image from a description: a picture, illustration, photo or graphic that
  does not exist yet. Returns the rendered image data itself rather than a description of one,
  and can take a reference photo to keep a person recognisable across several generations.
  Editing an image that already exists, and producing a fixed branded template, are different
  jobs.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NOT cacheable. Generation is non-deterministic, so asking twice is meant to produce two
  # different images, and reusing the first would be a bug rather than a saving.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# No reference photo, so this runs the one-call path. Asserts the SHAPE and that real bytes came
# back: base64 of any actual image is thousands of characters, so a length floor catches an
# empty or placeholder part without pinning anything about what was drawn.

testData:
  config:
    model: gemini-2.5-flash-image
    prompt: >-
      A serene mountain landscape at sunrise, photorealistic, golden-hour lighting, mist
      rolling over pine forests, wide-angle composition
    fileName: generated_image
    referenceImageUrl: ""
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    images: >-
      return output.images.length > 0
        && output.images[0].data.length > 1000
        && output.images[0].mimeType.startsWith('image/')
        && output.images[0].fileName === 'generated_image_0.png'
    text: "return typeof output.text === 'string'"
    metadata: >-
      return output.metadata.imageCount === output.images.length
        && output.metadata.model === 'gemini-2.5-flash-image'
        && output.metadata.generatedAt > 0
